autoresearch.research_question: When images are copied, collected, sounded, and entered rather than simply viewed, what kind of handmade world emerges on the screen?
autoresearch.synthesis: The strongest fresh material points toward an eccentric, image-led internet rather than a technology roundup. Planet Nerf's supermodel post supplies the clearest inspected artwork: four hazy cartoon-character panels, sunglasses, pink ears and hands, saturated blue backgrounds, red clothing, and smeared color. Zoomquilt offers a collaborative painting that can be entered indefinitely; Internet Flowers describes browsing history rebuilt as a garden of found images; Visual Instruments explicitly makes music out of images; Simone Conradi presents mathematical art and simulations. Together they suggest a soft, unstable picture-world assembled through repetition and small gestures. This is an editorial adjacency, not a claim that the artists share a movement. The viable shortlist remains below the requested source floor: several promising pages were recovered through extraction, but their image surfaces still need browser verification. Previously used music, synthetic recovery seeds, unresolved links, and tooling promotions should not fill the gap.
autoresearch.edition_thesis: Pictures with lives of their own: a provisional edition about repetition, accumulation, and playful image-worlds.
autoresearch.aesthetic_thesis: A hazy cartoon conservatory where smeared blue and pink forms, found-image blossoms, nested painted openings, and repeating curves become surfaces to explore.
visual_motifs: Soft cyan and cobalt fields interrupted by salmon pink and tomato red
Blurry color registration and rubbed, low-resolution edges
Dark sunglass-like slashes against rounded, pale forms
Repeated silhouettes that vary rather than align perfectly
Cutout blossoms gathered into uneven, overlapping beds
A painted opening nested inside another painted opening
Curved traces and repeating waves translated into material marks, not technical diagrams
Broad quiet spaces between image clusters, with source territories following actual painted boundaries
autoresearch.anchor_reason: Select https://x.com/planet_nerf/status/2052266270884855886 as the provisional editorial and visual anchor. Its attached raster was inspected directly: it is a four-panel cartoon montage, not a prompt guide, code screenshot, or model dashboard. The visible blur, exaggerated rounded anatomy, sunglasses, saturated clothing, and unstable color give the plate specific material grammar. The author's account of recursive training provides context, but selection rests on the artwork itself. Borrow its soft registration, chromatic instability, and repeated figures rather than reproducing its characters, weapons, or exact montage. The candidate is marked renderable and non-duplicate; full-archive parent/media clearance remains a downstream requirement.

clusters.label: Images remaking images
clusters.takeaway: The inspected supermodel artwork and the documented collaborative Zoomquilt offer two distinct forms of repetition: degraded variation and continuous spatial nesting.

clusters.label: Collecting becomes a place
clusters.takeaway: Internet Flowers turns the act of browsing into an image garden. Its saved description supplies unusually precise provenance and a coherent gathering gesture; the live floral surface still needs capture.

clusters.label: Images become instruments
clusters.takeaway: Visual Instruments explicitly connects images with sound, while Conradi's mathematical-art site offers a neighboring language of repetition and motion. Neither should be represented by controls, portraits, or explanatory text when the actual work can be captured.

source_decisions.why: Provisional anchor. Twitter bookmark dated 2026-05-08; candidate is fresh relative to its duplicate flag and renderable. Direct inspection confirms an original image-led cartoon montage with strong color and edge grammar. AI-assisted artwork is not equivalent to AI-tooling promotion.

Twitter bookmark dated 2026-06-19. Live extraction recovered the named collaborative infinitely zooming painting, its 2004 date, project lead, and participating illustrators. Strong spatial adjacency to recursive imagery; browser capture must establish a loaded painting rather than navigation or app-store badges.

Twitter bookmark dated 2026-04-26 describes a garden built from 999 flower images extracted from the artist's browsing history. A retry recovered the Internet Flowers title, but extraction did not expose the actual garden. Select provisionally for its specific artwork provenance, conditional on a real image-surface capture.

Twitter bookmark dated 2026-06-11. Live extraction identifies Visual Instruments as an exploration of making music out of images and exposes a sound-activation instruction. This adds a genuine musical gesture without importing spent recordings. Dynamic imagery, sound behavior, and mobile presentation remain unverified.

Twitter bookmark dated 2026-06-11. Live extraction identifies mathematical art, physics simulations, and computational explorations of mathematical beauty. A plausible source for repeating visual forms, but actual artwork must be captured; the extracted author portrait is not suitable source material.

Directly inspected attached image shows a sparse conceptual interface for finding numbers. Its absurd collecting premise supports the research question, but a text field and counter are too visually thin to justify a public window or dominant plate reference.

The August artwork collection is a promising recent saved signal and deserves priority in a recovery pass. Supplied evidence shows a security checkpoint and the new extraction failed. Do not infer lavender colors, game references, or any collection imagery from the title.

Live extraction recovered the artist-site title and digital/physical work categories, but not identifiable works or substantial image evidence. Keep as an investigation lead rather than padding the selected set.

Live extraction recovered a credible Detroit arts-center page with captions identifying gallery interiors, restored confessional booths, a library, nave, and transepts. Strong material source for another edition, but bringing it into this cartoon-and-browser world would stretch the connection.

Live extraction identifies Bilge Nur Saltik's Postmark Vase (Tall), 2025, and laser-cut aluminum, magnets, and a glass insert. Useful verified material detail, but actual object imagery was not recovered and its relationship to the selected world is weak.

Candidate evidence is challenge-page text and live extraction timed out. Do not invent textile texture, color, or an object image from the slug; also avoid multiplying one Detroit article's outbound links into artificial diversity.

Live extraction confirms a retro-game catalog, but the retrieved surface is chiefly platform navigation rather than a specific artwork or game scene. Do not import an unlisted game URL or use emulator chrome as visual material.

Live extraction confirms a branding archive with named projects. It remains a broad discovery page rather than a specific coherent source for this edition; its linked project pages are outside the candidate URL allowlist.

capture_notes: SOURCE FLOOR NOT MET: this is a five-source editorial shortlist, not a publish-ready selection. Four recovered web works remain conditional on real media capture. Return to candidate enrichment within the allowed saved-signal channels; do not pad the edition with duplicates, tooling, or generic cards.

Browser verification was blocked because the browser service was unreachable. Text extraction and direct inspection of the supermodel and Number Research rasters were completed; no browser screenshots, interaction tests, or media-preload proofs were produced.

For the anchor, retain the inspected four-panel source image as evidence. Capture the parent post and attribution, verify the media loads at useful resolution, and compare both parent status identity and attached image against the full archive before generation.

For Zoomquilt, capture the main painting at a specific recorded state after it loads. Exclude app-store badges, related-project thumbnails, and navigation. The original HTTP candidate string must remain the selected source identity; record any redirect separately.

For Internet Flowers, verify that the actual found-image garden renders. The extracted title and punctuation are not image proof. Capture a full composition and a close detail with visible flower boundaries; reject it if only a blank or loading surface appears.

For Visual Instruments, capture a working visual state after an intentional sound-activation gesture. Verify whether meaningful media can be represented in a source window without embedding the entire application. Test mobile separately because the page explicitly prefers a computer and landscape orientation.

For Conradi, identify and capture a real mathematical-art work visible on the allowed page, not the author portrait or an explanatory diagram. If its only useful works require new unlisted source URLs, withhold this window rather than inventing a candidate.

Prioritize a browser recovery attempt for Lavender Town when enrichment resumes, since it is a more recent saved artwork collection. Do not assign it a palette, style, or motif until the work itself is visible.
No fresh native YouTube selection survived the supplied duplicate and evidence gates. Do not report a native player, soundtrack, or embed-preload success for this shortlist.

Keep the plate image-only in live mode. Derive invisible hover and tap territories from actual forms and edges; use media-first source windows with compact attribution. Verify desktop and mobile windows for clipping and adequate width before publication.
rejected_patterns: Repeated parent works disguised as fresh Discogs pages, short links, alternate domains, authorless status URLs, or refreshed CDN images
Recently duplicated music uploads, artwork portfolios, illustrated archives, games, and interactive works
Tooling tutorials, agent infrastructure, model launches, prompt guides, code repositories, design-system exports, and SaaS promotions selected merely because a thumbnail exists
Unavailable YouTube embeds and generic channel or social-profile pages substituted for the specific saved work
Unresolved short links and opaque article locators promoted on the strength of captions alone
Malformed Instagram profile URLs silently repaired into different identifiers
404 pages, security checkpoints, and redirect stubs treated as rendered artworks
Synthetic recovery notes and emergency stock or documentation images treated as genuine creative consumption
Logos, portraits, badges, administrative forms, and interface controls used instead of the work
Unrelated material-rich objects or architectural photographs stitched into the thesis merely to reach a count
Assumed palettes or motifs derived from titles such as Lavender Town rather than inspected source imagery
Claims of channel diversity, screenshot proof, working embeds, or publication readiness unsupported by this research pass
autoresearch.workflow: aesthetic-field autoresearch: read all candidate source evidence, find the most visually fertile creative through-line, imagine the edition as a coherent aesthetic world, choose renderable source windows with provenance, and avoid infrastructure/tooling links unless they carry strong visible artifacts.
